# Generate has to work on a package that does not compile yet.
#
# Before it has run, main.go calls a TemplateRoutes that does not exist, so the
# package carries a type error. That is the normal starting state, not a
# problem, which is why the partial-AST warning covers syntax errors only: a
# type error leaves the source intact and merely incomplete, and warning about
# it would fire on every project's first generate.

! exec go build ./...
stderr 'undefined: TemplateRoutes'

muxt generate --use-receiver-type=T
! stderr 'warning: package has syntax errors'
exec go build ./...

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- template.gohtml --
{{- define "GET /greet Greet(ctx)" -}}
	{{- .Result -}}
{{- end -}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"context"
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"net/http"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templatesFS embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templatesFS, "*"))

type T struct{}

func (T) Greet(ctx context.Context) string { return "hello" }

// Routes is what a project writes before muxt has generated anything.
func Routes(mux *http.ServeMux) {
	TemplateRoutes(mux, T{})
}
